Title: Payroll System Update – Q3 Changes
Time: Thursday, 15 August 2025, 10:00–10:30
Description: Join a short walkthrough of the updated payroll deductions and how they appear on your payslip.

Title: Interview – Customer Support Specialist (L2)
Time: Monday, 19 August 2025, 14:00–15:00
Description: Final-round interview with Priya Raman for the L2 support role. The panel will cover her experience with order escalations and her approach to handling refund disputes.

Please review her CV beforehand; a copy is in the shared drive. We’ll also ask her to walk through a sample chat transcript where a customer is stuck on a delivery delay, so have one or two examples ready if you’d like to probe.

Note: the candidate mentioned she has used an AI assistant to help draft customer replies in a previous role. We’re not judging that per se, but we’d like to understand how she verifies accuracy before sending. That will be part of the conversation.

The meeting will be recorded for the hiring committee. If you can’t attend, let me know by Friday and I’ll reschedule.

Title: Recipe Blog Content Planning
Time: Wednesday, 21 August 2025, 11:00–12:00
Description: Brainstorming session for the new recipe blog series; bring your ideas for seasonal dishes.

Title: Hiring Interview – Jake Torres (Support Agent)
Time: Tuesday, 20 August 2025, 09:30–10:15
Description: First-round interview; please review the attached assessment before the call.

Title: Payroll Change – Direct Deposit Form Deadline
Time: Friday, 23 August 2025, 17:00
Description: Reminder that all direct deposit update forms for the September payroll cycle are due by end of day Friday. If you’ve changed banks or account numbers, please submit the form to People Ops. The automated tool in the HR portal will confirm receipt within one business day; if you don’t get a confirmation, email payroll@northstarretail.example. Late submissions will roll into the October cycle, so plan accordingly. No action is needed if your banking details haven’t changed.

intent.requested_action: Submit direct deposit form if changed

Title: Recipe Blog Photo Shoot
Time: Monday, 26 August 2025, 13:00–15:00
Description: Photoshoot for the autumn squash recipes; please bring the props discussed.

Title: Interview Debrief – Customer Support Specialist
Time: Monday, 19 August 2025, 16:00–16:45
Description: Let’s gather right after Priya’s interview to compare notes and decide on next steps. Please come with your ratings for each competency already entered in the scorecard; the hiring manager will pull them up during the meeting. We’ll spend the first ten minutes on the delivery-delay scenario, then discuss culture add and availability. If you’re on the fence about any answer, flag it so we can dig into specifics. The chatbot on the careers site will send candidates a status update only after we’ve all submitted feedback, so please have your notes in by end of day Tuesday.

Title: Recipe Blog Editorial Sync
Time: Thursday, 29 August 2025, 10:00–10:30
Description: Quick sync to finalize the September recipe line-up and assign writing slots. We’ll review the draft calendar in the shared sheet and confirm which recipes need testing before publication. Please note that the automated tool that checks for duplicate ingredients across posts is now live; if you see any false positives, send them to me. Also, we need to decide whether the pumpkin gnocchi post should go live before or after the apple galette. Come with your preferences.

Title: Payroll Update – New Overtime Codes
Time: Wednesday, 28 August 2025, 15:00–15:30
Description: Brief session on the new overtime codes in the payroll system; attendance recommended for all team leads.

Title: Recipe Blog Contributor Onboarding
Time: Friday, 30 August 2025, 10:00–11:00
Description: We’re welcoming two new contributors to the recipe blog next week, and this session will walk them through our style guide, photo requirements, and publishing workflow.

Please prepare a short overview of the tools we use. The automated tool that suggests tags for each recipe is a good example; show them how to review and edit those suggestions rather than accepting them blindly. Also, cover how to submit a draft for editing and what the typical turnaround is.

If you have examples of posts that did well and posts that needed heavy edits, bring one of each. We’ll leave time for questions at the end.
